lines: On my way uptown, I count the doors.
The window keeps my face for a while.
I can tell how late I am by the roofs.
At the coffee cart, I watch the light across the street.
At the top of the steps, the brass door is open.
In my notebook the whole trip fits on one line.
What did I put in the space between those words?
A spoon touches the rim. Twice.
There's another cup behind the one I took.
The door hangs open for the length of a breath.
Someone's hand is still on the other side.
I remember the brass. I don't remember the hand.
If you ask how long it takes to get here,
